The Quiet Hour

The old house stood at the end of the road, and every evening it felt beautiful and quiet. The family ate dinner together and talked about the day.

After the rain there was serendipity in the air — a faint petrichor that made the whole street seem ephemeral, almost gossamer, as if the moment might dissolve into pure tintinnabulation.

She kept studying for the exam because she wanted to observe how language slowly reveals itself, word by word.
